kubernetes-networking-under-the-hood.r: Calls to an external API took five seconds, but only from pods, because ndots:5 made the resolver try several cluster search suffixes first. Ending the name with a dot fixed it.
kubernetes-networking-under-the-hood.x: Read the endpoints, then the labels, then DNS. Most Kubernetes network problems are one of those three.

cni-network-policy-and-ebpf.r: A security review found a database reachable from every namespace even though a NetworkPolicy existed, because the cluster ran Flannel, which does not enforce policy at all.
cni-network-policy-and-ebpf.x: Pick a CNI that enforces policy, observe traffic first, allow DNS, add allows before default deny, and test that blocked traffic is really blocked.

what-a-service-mesh-is-and-how-it-works.r: After a control plane upgrade some proxies stayed on old config and returned 503s. Rolling the upgrade slowly and checking proxy-status avoided it later.
what-a-service-mesh-is-and-how-it-works.x: Adopt a mesh for a specific need, restart workloads after enabling injection, check proxy-status, and roll upgrades slowly.

mtls-and-traffic-management.r: Retries at three layers turned a slow database into a full storefront outage, because each user request became dozens of calls. Limiting retries to one layer and adding outlier detection fixed it.
mtls-and-traffic-management.x: Migrate with PERMISSIVE then STRICT, create DestinationRules before VirtualServices, run istioctl analyze, and keep retries at one layer.

observing-and-troubleshooting-the-mesh.r: Checkout failed even though every pod was Running, because 40 proxies were STALE after the control plane ran out of memory. istioctl proxy-status found the cause in seconds.
observing-and-troubleshooting-the-mesh.x: Check config sync first, read the flag, check endpoints and policies, and run more than one control plane replica.

sidecar-and-ambient-mesh-data-planes.r: A cluster with thousands of small pods spent more memory on sidecars than on the applications. Moving to a shared per-node model cut overhead and made upgrades less disruptive.
sidecar-and-ambient-mesh-data-planes.x: The data plane design sets your cost, blast radius and upgrade story. Pick it deliberately and measure the overhead before you commit a whole fleet.

ingress-gateways-and-the-gateway-api.r: Two teams edited one shared ingress object and broke each other's routes. Splitting into a platform-owned Gateway and per-team routes let each team change only its own rules.
ingress-gateways-and-the-gateway-api.x: The edge is where mistakes become public. Separate who owns the listener from who owns the routes, and review every change to exposed hosts and certificates.

traffic-shifting-retries-and-timeouts.r: A slow dependency caused every caller to retry three times. Load tripled on the struggling service and a small slowdown became an outage. Retry budgets and shorter timeouts stopped the storm.
traffic-shifting-retries-and-timeouts.x: Resilience features interact. Retries, timeouts and queues must be designed together from the user's deadline backwards.

mesh-authorization-and-zero-trust-policy.r: A flat network let any pod call the payments service. After identities and allow rules, only checkout could reach it, and a compromised test pod could no longer reach payment data.
mesh-authorization-and-zero-trust-policy.x: Zero trust means every call is authenticated and authorized, not just encrypted. Policy must be small, reviewed and observable, or teams will disable it to get work done.

multi-cluster-mesh-and-failover.r: A region failed and traffic moved to a second cluster that had no spare capacity. The failover worked as designed but overloaded the healthy side, so capacity planning became part of the design.
multi-cluster-mesh-and-failover.x: Multi-cluster improves availability only if failure domains stay independent. Shared control planes, shared certificates and shared capacity can quietly make two clusters fail together.

mesh-performance-cost-and-resource-tunin.r: The mesh worked in staging but proxies in a large cluster used gigabytes of memory because each knew about every service. Scoping configuration to the namespaces each workload used cut memory by 70 percent.
mesh-performance-cost-and-resource-tunin.x: Every feature has a per-request price. Collect only the telemetry you use, and make cost a visible metric of the platform.

operating-and-upgrading-a-service-mesh.r: An in-place control plane upgrade left proxies on an old version that could not understand new configuration. Traffic failed for some services until the team rolled back and adopted revision-based upgrades.
operating-and-upgrading-a-service-mesh.x: Treat the mesh like a database engine: version skew is a real risk. Upgrades must be reversible, staged and observed.
